title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Compass: you are the compass; keep growing and serving
summary: The chapter argues that when plans stop holding, a leader's real compass is their own capacity to grow, notice, shift and unlearn, not the strategy document. It urges turning discomfort into a growth signal, acting on lessons rather than collecting them, and choosing the people around you deliberately. It closes with a Thunder story: Thunder Talks, Bookclub and Thunder Lab are meant to build a circle of service, not an audience.

principles.text: A leader's real compass is their capacity to grow and adapt, not a precise plan.
principles.quote: The real compass is not the strategy document. It’s you. Your capacity to grow.

principles.text: People follow leaders who evolve and stay alive amid uncertainty, rather than defend yesterday's map.
principles.quote: Not how precise your plan is, but how alive you are in the face of uncertainty.

principles.text: Treat discomfort as a signal of growth: lean in rather than armor up.
principles.quote: To let the awkwardness be a teacher, not a threat.

principles.text: Learning only counts if it changes how you act; consuming content creates an illusion of growth.
principles.quote: Not “What should I know?” but “Who am I becoming?”

principles.text: Unlearn deliberately: question old beliefs and drives, especially when you feel most certain.
principles.quote: Growth doesn’t live in certainty. It lives in the willingness to question your own compass.

principles.text: Choose your circle with intention; Thunder builds spaces for growing together through service, not for audience.
principles.quote: We’re not trying to build an audience. We’re trying to build a circle.
